scale_004:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a draft of expense categories and spending limits for our company's expense management policy. This is a preparation task only — a finance leader must review and approve the actual dollar limits before anything is finalized.

Please do the following:

1. Ask me for any missing context: company size (headcount), industry, whether we're primarily remote/in-office/hybrid, current approximate monthly expense volume, and any existing expense policy documents I can share.
2. Draft a standard set of expense categories commonly used by companies of our size and industry — e.g., travel (airfare, lodging, ground transport), meals & entertainment, office supplies, software/subscriptions, client entertainment, professional development, home office equipment, and miscellaneous.
3. For each category, research and propose benchmark spending limits (per-transaction and/or monthly caps) based on typical industry practices for companies of similar size, clearly citing that these are benchmarks, not final numbers.
4. Note which categories typically require pre-approval versus post-expense reporting, and flag any categories that commonly need receipts above certain thresholds.
5. Compile all of this into a single clear draft document (table format: Category | Description | Suggested Limit | Approval Trigger | Notes) so finance leadership can review it quickly.
6. Explicitly call out that the dollar thresholds encode the company's financial risk tolerance and budget authority, and must be reviewed and set by a finance owner — do not present any numbers as final.

When the draft is ready, present it to me along with a short summary of your benchmarking sources/reasoning, and then stop for human sign-off. Do not attempt to load these limits into any system or treat any numbers as approved — this task ends once the draft and summary are ready for finance leadership's review.

scale_004:n2.prompt:
You are helping me configure per-employee card limits in {{vendor}}, our corporate card/expense platform, as part of setting up expense management. A human (me) must explicitly approve the final limits before they are applied to any card.

Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available, such as: our {{vendor}} login/dashboard access (use my configured credentials), the current employee roster with roles/departments, any existing department or program budget targets, and any known exceptions (e.g., higher limits for travel-heavy roles or executives).

Then do the following:
1. Pull the current list of employees with cards (or pending card issuance) in {{vendor}}, including their department, role, and any existing spend limits or controls.
2. Draft a proposed per-employee card limit table, grouping by department/role where sensible, and note any employees who may need virtual cards scoped to a specific vendor or purpose (e.g., ad spend) versus standard physical/digital cards.
3. Cross-check proposed limits against any department or program budget caps I've given you, flagging conflicts or employees whose proposed limit would exceed the department budget.
4. Prepare a clear summary document showing: current limits vs. proposed limits, rationale for each change, and total exposure per department.
5. Do NOT apply, save, or submit any limit changes in {{vendor}} — only prepare drafts and have them staged/ready in the interface if the tool allows saving as unpublished/draft.

Once your draft is ready, present the full proposed limit table and summary to me for review, and then stop for human sign-off. Do not click approve, confirm, or submit any changes yourself. Report back with: the proposed limits per employee, any flagged budget conflicts, and a short list of open questions or missing data that affected your recommendations.

scale_004:n3.prompt:
You are helping me set up approval workflows in {{vendor}}, our expense management platform, as part of configuring expense management for the company. If you don't already have it, ask me for: our {{vendor}} account access confirmation (I will confirm you can use my configured credentials), the org chart or list of teams/departments and their designated approvers, spending thresholds per role or department (e.g., manager approval under $X, finance-lead approval above), and any special routing rules (e.g., travel vs. software purchases, multi-level approval for large amounts).

Using that information, please:
1. In {{vendor}}, review current user roles and permissions and draft a proposed role/permission structure by team, department, and location, identifying who should be a submitter, approver, or finance-lead with one-click approve-and-pay authority.
2. Draft the expense approval rule(s) needed to route bills and expense reports through the correct approval chain before payment, based on the thresholds and routing logic I provide.
3. Prepare a clear written summary showing: proposed roles/permissions, proposed approval rules with thresholds, and which existing settings would change.
4. Enter the draft rules and role assignments into {{vendor}} in a staged/inactive state where possible so nothing goes live automatically, or note clearly if the platform requires immediate activation.

Do not activate, publish, or finalize any approval workflow, role change, or spending rule — this requires a human explicitly approving before changes are applied. Once your draft and summary are ready, present them to me for review and stop for human sign-off. In your report, include: the proposed role/permission table, the proposed approval rules with thresholds and routing logic, any conflicts or gaps you noticed (e.g., missing approver for a department), and a clear note that nothing has been activated pending my approval.

scale_004:n4.prompt:
You are helping me configure team-chat notifications for our expense management process. We use {{vendor}} as our team-chat tool. Please set up automated notifications so our finance and approval team sees real-time updates on expense events (new expense submitted, approval needed, approved, rejected, reimbursement processed).

Before starting, ask me for: (1) which {{vendor}} channel(s) should receive expense notifications, (2) which expense-related events should trigger a message (e.g., submission, approval request, approval/rejection, reimbursement completion), (3) any keyword or schedule-based filtering preferences so only relevant alerts interrupt the channel, and (4) whether we already have an incoming webhook URL configured in {{vendor}} for this channel, or if one needs to be created via the {{vendor}} dashboard or API.

Actions to take:
- Guide me through creating or locating the incoming webhook URL for the target channel(s) in {{vendor}}, using my configured credentials.
- Draft the notification rule logic that subscribes to the relevant expense events (via webhook or event subscription) and maps each event type to a clear, concise message format (include expense amount, submitter, status, and link if applicable).
- Configure per-channel tuning options in {{vendor}} (keyword filters, quiet hours/schedule) based on my stated preferences.
- Test the setup by sending a sample notification through the webhook to confirm formatting and delivery.

Done looks like: notification rules are configured and tested in {{vendor}}, messages post correctly to the designated channel(s), and filtering/schedule settings match my preferences.

Report back with: a summary of the events wired up, the channel(s) configured, the filtering/schedule rules applied, and the result of the test message (success/failure and any errors encountered).

scale_004:n5.prompt:
You are helping me finish the 'Document policy and share' step of setting up expense management. Goal: produce a clear, complete written expense policy document that captures our expense reporting process, approval workflows, corporate card rules, and reimbursement rules, then prepare it for distribution — but do NOT publish, email, or share it until I approve.

First, ask me for anything you don't already have: our company name, the expense tool(s) we're using for reporting and approvals, the approval workflow rules (who approves what dollar thresholds), corporate card policy details (limits, allowed categories, misuse consequences), reimbursement rules (submission deadlines, required receipts, payment timing), and where we want the policy stored (e.g., Google Docs, Notion, Confluence) and where we want it shared (e.g., Slack channel, email distribution list, company wiki).

Then draft a well-structured policy document with sections: Purpose, Expense Reporting Process, Approval Workflow, Corporate Card Policy, Reimbursement Rules, and Policy Violations/Exceptions. Write in plain, unambiguous language suitable for all employees. Prepare a short announcement message summarizing the policy for the sharing channel, and a checklist of where/how it will be posted once approved.

Do not create or publish anything live, send announcements, or upload the document to shared drives or channels. Compile the final draft document, the announcement text, and the distribution checklist, then stop for human sign-off before any of it is shared or applied.

Report back with: the full draft policy text, the draft announcement message, the proposed storage location and sharing channels, and a clear note that you are awaiting my approval before publishing or distributing anything.
